question.text: What risk-containment measures are available when trading in a particular commodity is causing excessive speculation and price distortion?

answer.text: Additional special and concentration margins, regulator-set position limits, DPL trading stops at limits, and SCRA powers to suspend business or prohibit undesirable speculation
SEBI has no authority to intervene
Only the exchange can take action
Traders must continue trading without any restrictions

explanation.text: The Logic: The source describes a set of risk-containment tools: additional special and concentration margins for market integrity, regulator-set position limits, daily price limit (DPL) trading stops when limits are hit, and SCRA powers to suspend stock exchange business or prohibit undesirable speculation. The Trap: The regulator does have intervention authority. Exchanges also act, but SCRA gives the regulator overriding power. Note: Treat these as a toolkit of risk-containment measures from the cited pages; the source does not prescribe a particular graduated or last-resort sequence.
